functions.name: readSkeletonData_drawOrderTimelines

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_drawOrderTimelines(Json* drawOrder_json, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw)
abi.drawOrder_json: the "drawOrder" JSON child. The parent B3 caches both spellings: "drawOrder" at 0x28d380 and the legacy "draworder" at 0x28eb30 (fallback block 0x28eb28-0x28eb40), and stores the winner in [sp+0x28] which B15 reads at 0x28e338/0x28e35c/0x28e5d4. Its +0x0c is the DECLARED frame count used twice: create's arg 0 (0x28e34c) and the duration index (0x28e5e4).
abi.data_raw: spSkeletonData* (parent [sp+0x18]); only +0x18 slotsCount is read (0x28e350 create arg 2, 0x28e3d0/0x28e3f0 size bases, 0x28e3fc/0x28e4c4/0x28e4e0 fill and tail bounds).
abi.animation_raw: spAnimation* (parent r11, saved to [sp+0x38] at 0x28e3b0 because r11 is reused for the line-442 array, restored at 0x28e5d0).
abi.return: DRAWORDER_TL_OK 1 (0x28e340 beq 0x28e614 or fall-through 0x28e610 -> 0x28e614), DRAWORDER_TL_HANDOFF_SLOT_NOT_FOUND 2 (0x28e464 beq 0x28e8ac, outside this module).

functions.semantics: drawOrder_json == NULL -> event block (0x28e338..0x28e340). Otherwise spDrawOrderTimeline_create(declared frame count, slotsCount) (0x28e344..0x28e354) and the handle is spilled to [sp+0x2c] (0x28e358). frame = node->child (0x28e35c/0x28e360); NULL goes straight to the publish tail (0x28e368 beq 0x28e5d4) so a zero-frame drawOrder still creates and publishes a timeline. After the frame loop the tail runs: count = animation->timelineCount (0x28e5dc), timelines = animation->timelines (0x28e5e0), declared = node->0x0c (0x28e5e4), timelineCount = count+1 stored FIRST (0x28e5e8/0x28e5ec), timelines[count] = timeline at the OLD cursor (0x28e5f4), last = times[declared-1] (0x28e5f8..0x28e600, FOUR-byte stride), duration = max(duration, last) via vcmpe/vmrs/vmovgt (0x28e604..0x28e610).
functions.key_note: the two spellings are resolved by the parent B3 block (0x28d380 / 0x28eb28..0x28eb40), not here; this module receives the winning node.

field_offsets.spSkeletonData.slotsCount: +0x18 (0x28e350; corroborated by spSkeletonData_findSlotIndex 0x28b0d4 which loads the same word as its own count)

tail.stride: FOUR bytes per frame: 0x28e5fc add r3,r3,r2,lsl#2 then 0x28e600 vldr s15,[r3,#-4] -> times[declared-1]. This is the sharpest difference from the path family's two-float stride (0x28e030 add r3,r3,r2,lsl#3 / [r3,#-8]).
tail.cursor: the count is written before the element store, and the element store uses the pre-increment r3 (the OLD count), so the timeline lands at timelines[count] while timelineCount becomes count+1.
tail.declared_vs_child: the loop follows the child list; create and the duration index both use the declared count, so declared=3 with one frame reads times[2] (never written, zero) and keeps duration 0.

quirks: A zero-frame drawOrder object still creates and publishes a timeline: 0x28e354 create runs BEFORE the 0x28e368 child test.
declared == 0 makes the tail index times[0xffffffff] (0x28e5fc add with r2 = 0 then vldr [r3,#-4]); the original reads it blindly and the fixture never drives it.
The duration compare is vcmpe + vmrs + vmovgt, i.e. strictly greater wins, so a NaN last time keeps the old duration.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_drawOrderTimelineFrames

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_drawOrderTimelineFrames(Json* drawOrder_json, void* data_raw, void* timeline_raw)
abi.return: DRAWORDER_TL_OK or the slot-miss handoff (propagated from the per-frame builder).

functions.semantics: frame = drawOrder_json->child (0x28e360); NULL -> OK with no setFrame (0x28e368). frameIndex = 0 (0x28e370 mov r10,#0). Per frame (head 0x28e3b4, back edge 0x28e5cc): readSkeletonData_drawOrderFrame (0x28e3b4..0x28e528, or the 0x28e590 join), time = Json_getFloat(frame,"time",0.0f) (0x28e594..0x28e5a0), spDrawOrderTimeline_setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, order) (0x28e5a4..0x28e5b8), _free(order) (0x28e5bc/0x28e5c0), frameIndex++ (0x28e5ac), frame = frame->next (0x28e5c4).
functions.no_readcurve: census §2.9 says the 8 readCurve call sites do not include this family, and the checker proves it by scanning every aligned word of the three translated windows: the BL set is exactly {create, setFrame, _malloc x2, _free x2, Json_getItem, Json_getString, Json_getFloat, Json_getInt, findSlotIndex, setError, spAnimation_dispose} and no BL targets the anonymous readCurve entry 0x28b34c. This module therefore has no readCurve link gate.
functions.register_note: r9 = frame, r4 = offsets node then reused as `original`, r7 = offsets entry, r11 = the line-442 array, r6 = the line-445 array, r5 = `unmoved`, r8 = data, r10 = frameIndex. r11 (the animation pointer) is spilled to [sp+0x38] at 0x28e3b0 and restored at 0x28e5d0 because the line-442 malloc reuses r11.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_drawOrderFrame

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_drawOrderFrame(Json* frame, void* data_raw, int32_t** out_order)
abi.out_order: the line-445 array (B) or NULL when the frame has no "offsets". The CALLER owns it: it must reach spDrawOrderTimeline_setFrame and then be _free'd exactly once (0x28e5c0).
abi.return: DRAWORDER_TL_OK 1, or DRAWORDER_TL_HANDOFF_SLOT_NOT_FOUND 2 with BOTH arrays still allocated (the original jumps to 0x28e8ac without a _free — the leak is reproduced, not repaired).

functions.semantics: offsets = Json_getItem(frame,"offsets") (0x28e3b4..0x28e3bc); absent -> *out_order = 0 (0x28e3c0 beq 0x28e590, where r4 == 0). n = offsets->+0x0c (0x28e3c8). A = _malloc((slotsCount - n)*4, tag, 442) (0x28e3cc..0x28e3e0); B = _malloc(slotsCount*4, tag, 445) (0x28e3e8..0x28e3f8); B is filled with -1 for exactly slotsCount words, skipped entirely when slotsCount <= 0 (0x28e3fc..0x28e420). original = 0, unmoved = 0 (0x28e42c..0x28e43c). Per offsets entry (head 0x28e440, back edge 0x28e4c0): name = Json_getString(entry,"slot",NULL) (0x28e44c), slotIndex = spSkeletonData_findSlotIndex(data,name) (0x28e458), -1 -> handoff (0x28e45c/0x28e464); if slotIndex != original, A[unmoved++] = original..slotIndex-1 (0x28e46c..0x28e48c) and original = slotIndex (0x28e498); offset = Json_getInt(entry,"offset",0) (0x28e4a8); B[original+offset] = original (0x28e4b4/0x28e4b8); original++ (0x28e4bc). After the list, every slot index not mentioned is appended to A (0x28e4c4..0x28e4f0, SIGNED bound). The merge walks B from the tail (0x28e4f4/0x28e4fc), and every -1 is replaced by A[--unmoved] (0x28e500..0x28e514), then A is _free'd (0x28e520/0x28e524) and B is returned.

malloc_442.size: (slotsCount - jsonOffsetsSize) * 4 via 0x28e3d8 rsb r0,r3,r0 and 0x28e3dc lsl r0,r0,#2 — both 32-bit wrap
malloc_442.ownership: caller-owned scratch; freed at 0x28e524 INSIDE this function, before setFrame ever sees anything; never escapes

malloc_445.size: slotsCount * 4 via 0x28e3f0 ldr r0,[r8,#0x18] + 0x28e3f4 lsl r0,r0,#2
malloc_445.fill: every one of the slotsCount words is set to -1: 0x28e40c mvnpl r0,#0 ; 0x28e418 str r0,[r2,#-0x4]! ; 0x28e420 bne 0x28e414. The count comes from 0x28e400 subs r1,r2,#1 and the loop stops at cmn r1,#1, i.e. exactly slotsCount stores; slotsCount <= 0 skips the fill (0x28e410 bmi).
malloc_445.ownership: caller-owned; passed to setFrame (0x28e5b4/0x28e5b8) and freed IMMEDIATELY AFTER the call (0x28e5bc/0x28e5c0). setFrame deep-copies it (line 690), so nothing of the caller's buffer survives inside the timeline.

merge.run_copy: 0x28e46c subne r1,r5,#-1073741823 ; 0x28e474 addne r1,r11,r1,lsl#2 ; 0x28e480 str r2,[r1,#0x4]! — the #0x3FFFFFFF immediate tricks computes A + r5*4 - 4, then the pre-increment write-back lands on A[r5]; the run length is (slotIndex - original) and `unmoved` is advanced by that same amount at 0x28e490/0x28e494.
merge.tail_fill: 0x28e4d0..0x28e4f0 uses the same trick to append original..slotsCount-1 after the last entry.
merge.merge_direction: 0x28e4f4 subs r1,r2,#1 ; 0x28e4f8 addpl r2,r6,r2,lsl#2 ; then the loop pre-decrements B and consumes A from the top (0x28e50c subeq r5,r5,#1 ; 0x28e510 ldreq r3,[r11,r5,lsl#2]), so the leftover slots keep their ascending order in the final array.
merge.signed_bounds: the tail-fill bound is SIGNED (0x28e4cc bge) and the merge is skipped when slotsCount <= 0 (0x28e4fc bmi).

quirks: A slot named exactly as the previous one does not extend the run (0x28e478 beq 0x28e49c), it only writes B[slotIndex+offset] and advances original.
A miss leaks BOTH arrays: the only exit to 0x28e8ac is the conditional branch at 0x28e464 and no _free precedes it on that path.
jsonOffsetsSize > slotsCount hands _malloc a wrapped size ((slotsCount - n) << 2); reproduced as-is and pinned by the fixture (slotsCount 2, declared 3 -> request 0xfffffffc).

If slotIndex < original the run loop at 0x28e47c never terminates (the index walks away from slotIndex through the 32-bit space) and A overruns; the original has no guard and the fixture does not drive it.

data->slotsCount is READ FIVE TIMES (0x28e3d0 for A's base, 0x28e3f0 for B's size, 0x28e3fc for the fill count, 0x28e4c4 and 0x28e4e0 for the tail bound). The translation keeps each read at its own site instead of caching one value, and the fixture's slots_count_reload test mutates the word inside the line-442 allocator callback to prove the difference: A is sized from 3, B from 2.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_attachmentNotFound

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_attachmentNotFound(Json* attachmentNode, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw, void* parser_raw)

functions.semantics: spAnimation_dispose(animation) (0x28e570) -> _spSkeletonJson_setError(parser, NULL, "Attachment not found: ", attachmentNode->name) (0x28e574..0x28e588) -> spSkeletonData_dispose(data) (0x28da48) -> return NULL.
functions.trigger: the ONLY edge into the block is 0x28e10c subs r8,r0,#0 ; 0x28e110 beq 0x28e55c, inside the DEFORM block: spSkin_getAttachment(skin, slotIndex, timelineNode->name) (0x28e108) returned NULL. So the block belongs to the deform family but sits in this module's address window (census §6 puts it between B15 and B15b).
functions.json_argument: NULL, proven twice: statically, r5 = r8 at 0x28e55c and r8 can only be 0 on the single edge that reaches the block (0x28e10c subs r8,r0,#0 ; 0x28e110 beq); the fixture then shows that no Json node is disposed and parser->error still gets the formatted text. This is the NULL form (the slots family's E1 shape), not the animation-node form used by the bones/path families.
functions.extra_string: 0x28e580 ldr r3,[r7,#0x1c] where r7 = r9 = the attachment timeline node, so the message carries the attachment NAME (its member key), not a slot name.

layout_additions.spSkeletonData: +0x18 int32 slotsCount (this module + spSkeletonData_findSlotIndex 0x28b0d4); the slot vector itself is +0x1c (0x28b0e0), already used by c/skeleton_find

ownership_open4.question: census §7 open #4: line 442 (slotsCount - jsonOffsetsSize)*4 and line 445 slotsCount*4 (filled -1) — which one reaches spDrawOrderTimeline_setFrame, which one is _free'd, and in which branch?
ownership_open4.answer: NEITHER pointer is retained by the timeline. Line 442 (A) is a scratch array that never leaves readSkeletonData_drawOrderFrame: it is _free'd at 0x28e524 after the leftover merge and BEFORE setFrame is called. Line 445 (B) is the drawOrder array: it is passed as setFrame's 4th argument at 0x28e5b8 and _free'd immediately afterwards at 0x28e5c0. setFrame does not keep it either — 0x282e24 _malloc(slotsCount*4, tag, 690) plus 0x282e44 memcpy into the timeline's own drawOrders[i], after freeing the slot's previous pointer at 0x282e00.
freed_by_reader: A at 0x28e524 (0x285c80), inside the offsets-present branch, before setFrame
B at 0x28e5c0 (0x285c80), after every setFrame call, including when B is NULL (no "offsets" member -> 0x28e590 sets r6 = 0)
freed_by_setFrame: the previous drawOrders[i] at 0x282e00 (NULL on the first call, so _free(0) is forwarded)
ownership_open4.not_freed_on_the_miss_path: 0x28e464 beq 0x28e8ac leaves A and B allocated; the original has no _free between 0x28e3e0/0x28e3f8 and that branch, so both leak. The fixture asserts the leak instead of repairing it.
ownership_open4.evidence: checker teeth free_a_dropped / free_b_dropped / free_b_before_setframe plus the single_entry_identity free-sequence assertion (A is ff[0], setFrame's NULL slot is ff[1], B is ff[2]).

The drawOrder ABI of spDrawOrderTimeline_create/setFrame is read from their bodies (0x282d4c/0x282ddc) and modelled synthetically; whether spDrawOrderTimeline_apply (not recovered) interprets drawOrders[i] == 0 as "no change for this frame" is not proven here.

slotsCount <= 0 is only reached through the create/size paths; the -1 fill and the merge are skipped, but what the allocator returns for a zero-byte request is the fixture's business, not the original's.

jsonOffsetsSize > slotsCount is recorded (0xfffffffc request) but not explained: whether a shipped skeleton can carry an offsets array longer than the slot count needs an asset; no spine JSON exists in this tree.
slotIndex < original makes the run loop at 0x28e47c non-terminating with an unbounded A write; recorded as bytes, not driven.
declared frame count == 0 makes the publish tail read times[0xffffffff]; recorded, not driven (same restriction as the other timeline modules).

E4 is driven directly by the fixture. Its real trigger (spSkin_getAttachment returning NULL inside the deform block at 0x28e108) belongs to the deform family and is not part of this module's runtime path.
